title: Grateful Dead Live at Assembly Hall, U. of Il. on 1973-02-22

ai_review.summary: A crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a fiery Feb 1973 show, highlighted by an explosive Dark Star > Eyes > China Doll sequence and soaring Birdsong.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its crisp, headphone‑ready mix that lets the band’s 1973 peak shine through.  Fans repeatedly point to the incendiary Dark Star→Eyes→China Doll jam, the lush Birdsong, Playin’ and Box of Rain as show‑highlights, while the second set flows with tight transitions and high energy.  Overall the performance is described as tight, humorous, and at the top of the year’s Dead outings.

ai_rating.rationale: 19 reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 4‑5 stars; comments are consistently enthusiastic about both performance and sound quality, giving a solid average of ~4.4.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix that sounds amazing on headphones; reviewers note it as ‘standing strong’ and ‘clean, strong sound’, with only occasional remarks of “slightly above average” but no serious flaws.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Second set is praised for seamless jams and transitions; the band rides a high‑energy wave from Dark Star into Eyes, then into China Doll, with tight rhythm section work and vibrant improvisations throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly described as making his guitar ‘sing’, delivering bubbling wah‑wah riffs, laser‑like leads, and jazzy/funky textures that drive the jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: His bass is called “tasty” and he provides strong vocal work on Box of Rain; reviewers note the rhythm section (Phil, Jerry, Keith) bouncing beats off each other and propelling the music.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted as missing from the first‑set mix but audible in the second set; no specific performance praise beyond that.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s keyboards are highlighted for weaving counterpoint with Jerry, adding jazzy layers and enhancing the overall weave of the band.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drumming is praised for driving the train on jams like Dark Star and Eyes, providing solid rhythmic foundation.
